summary: The first divergence is a missed kobold dart attack. In weapon.c select_rwep(), negative weapon skills outside bow, sling and crossbow retain hands_obj as their propellor, so darts and shuriken need no launcher. JavaScript launcherFor() returns null for those skills and select_rwep() skips the weapon; repair that branch of the complete selection function and preserve its caller contracts.

source.branch: The ranged-weapon preference loop reaches a dart or shuriken with negative oc_skill, an eligible inventory object, and no welded weapon prohibiting the throw. C weapon.c:627-650 initializes gp.propellor to &hands_obj, then replaces it only for P_BOW, P_SLING or P_CROSSBOW; the unmatched negative skill retains the sentinel. At the examined first divergence, an unconfused hostile kobold carries nine darts, has no wielded weapon, and is aligned with the approaching hero. JavaScript launcherFor() defaults to null, and select_rwep() continues before selecting the dart.
callers: C mthrowu.c thrwmu():1184-1194 invokes mon_wield_item() and select_rwep(); its selected missile reaches monshoot():1259 and monmulti(). JavaScript js/unported_monster_actions.js throwRangedWeapon():1394-1428 dispatches to js/mthrowu.js thrwmu():1531-1600, which uses select_rwep for both its launcher side result and its missile result.

Production attack path: monmove.c dochug() permits a non-nearby AT_WEAP monster to shoot after moving, then mhitu.c mattacku() dispatches its range2 AT_WEAP arm to thrwmu(). Corresponding JavaScript gates are js/monmove.js:2579-2620 and js/mhitu.js:945-952, through attackHeroWithMattacku().

Other consumed selection callers are C mthrowu.c thrwmm():984, weapon.c mon_wield_item():814 and monmove.c dochug():855; JavaScript js/mthrowu.js:1255-1266 and js/monmove.js wield_pre_move_weapon() use the same selection and propellor contract. Preserve them while repairing the shared function.
dependencies: include/objects.h:160-165 defines DART with -P_DART and SHURIKEN with -P_SHURIKEN. js/weapon.js RANGED_WEAPONS includes both; no species or session exception is needed.

js/weapon.js launcherFor():615-629 is an extracted part of C select_rwep(), not a separate source unit. Its default result must preserve the C hands_obj choice while missing bow, sling and crossbow launchers still yield null.

C oselect(), can_touch_safely(), mwelded(), m_carrying(), object skill data and the ranged preference order govern which candidate is returned. Verify the entire select_rwep() function at weapon.c:533-676 and its consumed return values; preserve artifact, welded, loadstone, gem, polearm and return-weapon branches.

hands_obj flows through propellorResult to mon_wield_item(), whose no-launcher-needed path consumes no wield turn. thrwmu() then selects the missile again, checks lined_up() and retreat conditions, and enters existing monshoot()/monmulti()/m_throw() behavior. The observed annotation names the first missing RNG call rather than the defective owner.

This isolates the selection error without modifying game behavior or running a fresh C recording.

The actionable whole-unit scope is a divergence fix in weapon.c select_rwep() and its JavaScript launcherFor extraction, with existing caller wiring retained and verified. Extend the existing source-pinned selection tests in scripts/weapon.test.mjs:290-370 to cover launcher-free negative skills, their preference order, and the welded exclusion; existing dagger and arrow fixtures do not cover that switch default. The 227-screen upper bound is scheduling provenance, not a predicted gain. This investigation establishes the first missing attack; later potion_dip and extended-command stops remain outside this scope, and no post-fix parity or aggregate score is claimed.
